"Mistral Large 4" 

paper published exclusively on alphaXiv

Their latest technical report shares that aggressively reducing KV-cache memory can hurt an LLM's agentic capabilities, even when its language modeling performance looks unchanged.

Mistral initially reduced KV-cache memory by 16x, but they found that this hurts long-context agentic tasks, where models need to retrieve information from much earlier context.

To fix this, Mistral restored full-context attention to more layers, then adopted DeepSeek Sparse Attention to select the 2,048 most relevant tokens across the context instead of attending to everything.

Their resulting 1T-parameter MoE model (w 52B active) scores 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 19.7% on FrontierCode 2.0, and its NVFP4-quantized checkpoint fits on four GB300 GPUs.

https://t.co/L3pESAejPt

"Multi-Token Prediction Done Right"

Multi-token prediction (MTP) helps LLMs predict a few future tokens, but this paper finds that around 80% of its training gradient comes from a noisy component that interferes with learning.

They introduce Soft-MTP, which removes this noisy gradient and instead trains MTP heads to match the model's own next-token predictions. This change requires just one line of code, with no additional parameters or measurable training overhead.

Across 167M-1.2B models, Soft-MTP improves perplexity, downstream accuracy, and speculative decoding speed. 

At 1.2B, HumanEval Pass@64 improves from 40.85% to 43.90%, while speculative decoding becomes roughly 1.5% faster than standard MTP

https://t.co/QM4rawWYGP
Check out this work from @rikiyatakehi @jayden_teoh_ @a1zhang @lateinteraction on alphaXiv! https://t.co/XAozMNrVdL

tweets.text:
The divergence in AI output weirdly may be the highest it’s ever been, even though adoption is the broadest it’s ever been. 

A few years ago the best productivity gains you could get, even in the most capability-aligned field (like coding), was maybe 30-50% better productivity if you were very good at it. You’d spend a decent chunk of time cleaning up the mistakes of models, the context windows were too limited to do any long running work, and the interfaces required highly synchronous interactions. 

Now, the models can do far longer tasks at a time with limited human interaction. The harnesses support agentic work that can take on these larger tasks. The models are trained on vastly better datasets for a growing array of domains so you have to intervene far less. And we have systems that better support working with many agents at once. 

In just a two year timespan, the upper limits on productivity gains have gone from 30-50% to now likely 5-10X depending on the field. So we’ve gone from an environment where living at the frontier vs. not paying attention at all could be an order of magnitude difference in your output.

This distance is only getting wider from here given the rate of progress we’re likely to see with RSI. Crazy times.
